ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that lines $AB$ and $CD$ intersect at point $O$, and $\angle COE=90^\circ$. If $\angle BOD:\angle BOC = 3:6$, what is the degree measure of $\angle AOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}

Given that $\angle BOD : \angle BOC = 3 : 6$,\\
and $\angle BOD + \angle BOC = 180^\circ$,\\
hence, $\angle BOD = 60^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle BOD = \angle AOC$,\\
it follows that $\angle AOC = 60^\circ$,\\
Given $\angle COE = 90^\circ$,\\
thus, $\angle AOE = \angle COE + \angle AOC = 90^\circ + 60^\circ = \boxed{150^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are two straight lines AB and CD intersecting at point O; CD is a horizontal straight line, C is to the left of O, and D is to the right of O; AB is an oblique straight line, A is at the lower left, and B is at the upper right; OE goes upward from O, and the right-angle mark in the figure indicates that OE is perpendicular to CD, so ∠COE=90°. From the image, ∠AOE is the angle from OA through OC and then to OE, so it can be divided into ∠AOC and ∠COE. Then reason: It is known that ∠BOD:∠BOC=3:6. Because OC and OD are opposite rays, ∠BOD and ∠BOC form a straight angle, and their sum is 180°. The total number of proportional parts is 3+6=9, and each part is 180°/9=20°, so ∠BOD=3×20°=60°. Also because ∠BOD and ∠AOC are vertical angles, ∠AOC=60°. It is known that ∠COE=90°, and ∠AOE=∠AOC+∠COE, so ∠AOE=60°+90°=150°.
